methodologyNotes: Roster covers 12 OTC TENS/EMS units a 2026 buyer typically compares, spanning budget wired units through app-controlled wireless systems: TENS 7000 2nd Edition, Omron Pocket Pain Pro (PM400, the current SKU that superseded the PM3029/PM3030), Omron Max Power Relief (PM500), iReliev ET-1313, Compex Edge 3.0, AUVON Dual Channel TENS Unit, Belifu Dual Channel TENS/EMS Unit, NueMedics Tens 24, HealthmateForever YK15AB, Easy@Home EHE009, and PowerDot 2.0 Duo, plus TechCare Massager Plus 24 added for category coverage. Primary sources were official manufacturer pages (tens7000.com, omronhealthcare.com) where reachable, cross-checked against medgrade.org's per-device spec tables (fetched and parsed from raw HTML, not just AI summaries) and, for iReliev ET-1313, a manufacturer product-box photo that visually confirmed model number, program count and timer text. Four brand storefronts — ireliev.com, nuemedics.com, auvonhealth.com and techcaremassager.com — were unreachable all session (network layer returned 429 'local_rate_limited' on every attempt, including plain product-JSON endpoints), so those four products relied on medgrade.org plus archived manual/retail listings instead; NueMedics additionally has no confirmed USD price or intensity-level count (both left null) because no reachable source published either. One QA note worth flagging: a '100 intensity levels' figure for PowerDot 2.0 Duo turned out on raw-text review to be the device's peak 100 mA output current, not a discrete intensity-level count, so intensity_levels is null for PowerDot rather than a mA figure mislabeled as levels. For the Compex Edge 3.0, the medgrade.org spec table does list 'Intensity Levels: 999' (confirmed in the live page), which is Compex's genuine 0-999 intensity scale, so that field is recorded as 999. AUVON's medgrade listing carries FDA/regulatory model number TP2208C while its retail packaging and manual (ManualsLib-hosted) use AS8012; both names are for the same physical dual-channel unit and are noted together. 'electrode_pads_included' reflects pads shipped in the base box, not replacement-pad multipacks (several device pages list a monthly/replacement pad SKU under a cost-analysis section that is NOT the in-box count, and was excluded accordingly). All prices are current US list/street price for the base single-unit configuration; accessedAt 2026-08-01.

products.name: TENS 7000 2nd Edition
products.priceNote: MSRP for the 2nd Edition kit with accessories on tens7000.com (the brand's own storefront); a bare-bones listing at tensproducts.com shows $36.95 for the same device without the full accessory kit
products.provenance: Fetched directly from tens7000.com: dual channel (up to 4 electrodes), 0-100 mA output across 8 intensity levels, 5 built-in modes (Normal, Burst, Modulation, SD1, SD2), pulse duration 50-300 µs, timer adjustable 2-60 min, 9V battery, four 2"x2" reusable electrodes included, FDA-cleared OTC device. Product photo (downloaded and visually confirmed) shows the branded hard case, 2 lead wires, 4 pads and the dual-channel LCD unit reading CH1/CH2, 120 Hz, SD2, 60 Min.

specs.preset_modes: 5 (3 pain-relief programs: Arm/Shoulder, Lower Back, Leg/Foot + 2 massage modes: Knead, Steady)

products.provenance: Fetched directly from omronhealthcare.com: single-channel, 10 adjustable intensity levels, 3 pre-set pain programs (Arm/Shoulder, Lower Back, Leg/Foot) plus 2 massage modes (Knead, Steady), 2 AAA batteries, 2 reusable Long Life Pads included (reusable up to ~150 uses), max 15-minute therapy duration, belt-clip design. Page did not itself state an FDA clearance line; fda_cleared confirmed via the device's registered AccessGUDID/UDI entry (Omron Healthcare, model PM400), and OTC TENS devices legally require FDA 510(k) clearance to be sold in the US. Product photo downloaded and visually confirmed (round silver 'OMRON' unit, 2 Long Life Pads).

products.priceNote: Current price per medgrade.org device page; other retailers have shown this model between $49.95 and $67.95 list
products.provenance: TENS-only (no EMS) wired dual-channel device: 80 mA medical-grade symmetrical biphasic output, 8 pre-set programs, dual-channel with independent per-channel intensity, 3 AAA batteries, FDA 510(k) Cleared (confirmed in medgrade.org raw page text). Downloaded and visually confirmed the retail box photo, which reads 'Model # ET-1313', 'Wired', '8 TENS Programs', '60 Minutes Adjustable Therapy Time', and shows the LCD reading CH1 25 / CH2 25 / P8 TENS / 60 MIN — corroborating the 25-level intensity figure and the up-to-60-minute timer. ireliev.com itself was unreachable all session (429 on every request, including the .json product endpoint); iReliev's own official site could not be used as the primary source this pass. Box-included electrode pad count not confirmed anywhere reached (only a separate 4-8 pad refill-kit SKU was found) — left null rather than guessed.

products.name: Compex Edge 3.0
products.priceNote: List price per medgrade.org (data-track-price=149.99, matches the on-page displayed $149.99); street price at some retailers (e.g. Medco Sports Medicine) runs closer to $139.72

specs.power_source: rechargeable Li-ion battery (USB), up to 8 hrs of stimulation

products.provenance: Verified directly against medgrade.org's raw HTML spec table: 'Number of Channels: 4 independent channels', 'Pre-set Programs: 4 (Resistance, Strength, Recovery, TENS)', 'Intensity Levels: 999', 'Power Source & Battery Life: Rechargeable battery; up to 8 hours', 'FDA Classification: Class II Medical Device', device price $149.99. The 999 figure is the source-listed value and matches Compex's signature 0-999 intensity scale used across its stimulator line, so intensity_levels is recorded as 999. Electrode pad count (2x 2"x4" + 4x 2"x2" = 6 total) and timer behavior are corroborated by Medco Sports Medicine's product page (which lists 2x4 snap electrodes qty 2 + 2x2 snap electrodes qty 4); Compex Edge 3.0 uses fixed program durations rather than a user-set timer dial, so timer_range_min is left null. No wireless/app connectivity on this wired model. compexusa.com now redirects to the brand's French storefront and could not be used directly this pass.
